subject.title: ci(cloudflare): deploy crawl-remote from protected ClawSweeper environment

question: Must crawl-remote production deployment require independent, non-bypassable environment approval, or is the current single-operator self-approval boundary intentionally acceptable?
rationale: The workflow code is internally coherent, but the live environment allows admin bypass and self-review by its sole reviewer; only repository owners can decide whether that is an acceptable production authorization model.

options.title: Require independent approval
options.body: Disable self-review where possible, add a separate authorized approver, constrain bypass policy, and verify the main-only branch rule before production use.

options.title: Accept single-operator control
options.body: Explicitly accept that the named operator can dispatch and approve deployment, with documented auditing, succession, and emergency procedures.

options.title: Keep deployment external
options.body: Do not merge this repository-controlled production path if neither authorization model is acceptable.

recommendation.title: Require independent approval
recommendation.body: Disable self-review where possible, add a separate authorized approver, constrain bypass policy, and verify the main-only branch rule before production use.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice concerns repository-wide production authorization policy, and his history shows foundational ownership of the surrounding workflow control plane; Vincent Koc is the implementation owner and likely co-reviewer.
